newsitem.title: USA: W.R. Grace sells cocoa unit to ADM for $430 million.
newsitem.headline: W.R. Grace sells cocoa unit to ADM for $430 million.

text.p: W.R. Grace & Co. said Monday it agreed to sell its cocoa business to Archer Daniels Midland Co. for $430 million in cash.
The sale is part of Grace's previously announced plan to sell non-core businesses and to focus on its packaging and speciality chemicals businesses.
The unit, based in Stamford, Conn., produces and sells industrial cocoa and chocolate products. Grace Cocoa has operations in Europe, North and South America, Africa and Asia Pacific.

"Grace Cocoa is an outstanding business and we are delighted that we have been able to find such a fitting new home for its management and personnel, said Grace Chief Executive and President Albert J. Costello.
"This divestiture further advances our strategy to focus on Grace's global market-leading packaging and speciality chemicals businesses," he said.
The acquisition will give Archer Daniels Midland Co., an agricultural giant, its first entry into the industrial cocoa and chocolate business.

"There are a few key factors which make this purchase a good fit for us," said ADM's chairman, Dwayne O. Andreas. "We understand the procurement and processing business and have many customers in common."
Grace's stock jumped $1.625 to $50.25 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange, while ADM was down 12.5 cents at $22.25, also on the NYSE.
